{{Short description|Statistical measure of centrality}}
In [[statistics]], the '''pseudomedian''' is a measure of [[central tendency|centrality]] for data-sets and populations. It agrees with the [[median (statistics)|median]] for symmetric data-sets or populations. In [[mathematical statistics]], the pseudomedian is also a [[location parameter]] for [[probability distribution]]s.

==Description==

The pseudomedian of a distribution <math>F</math> is defined to be a median of the distribution of <math>(Z_1+Z_2)/2</math>, where <math>Z_1</math> and <math>Z_2</math> are independent, each with the same distribution <math>F</math>.<ref>{{cite book |last=Hollander |first=M. |last2=Wolfe |first2=D. A. |last3=Chicken |first3=E. |year=2014 |title=Nonparametric Statistical Methods |edition=3rd |page=58 |isbn=978-0-470-38737-5 }}</ref>

When <math>F</math> is a symmetric distribution, the pseudomedian coincides with the [[median]]; otherwise this is not generally the case. For example, the median of an exponential distribution of rate 1 is about 0.693, while its pseudomedian is about 0.839.

The [[Hodges–Lehmann estimator|Hodges–Lehmann statistic]], defined as the median of all of the midpoints of pairs of observations, is a [[consistent estimator]] of the pseudomedian.

Like the set of medians, the pseudomedian is well defined for all probability distributions, even for the many distributions that lack modes or means.

==Pseudomedian filter in signal processing==

In [[signal processing]] there is another definition of '''pseudomedian filter''' for discrete signals.

For a time series of length 2''N''&nbsp;+&nbsp;1, the pseudomedian is defined as follows. Construct ''N''&nbsp;+&nbsp;1 sliding windows each of length&nbsp;''N''&nbsp;+&nbsp;1. For each window, compute the minimum and maximum. Across all ''N''&nbsp;+&nbsp;1 windows, find the maximum minimum and the minimum maximum. The pseudomedian is the average of these two quantities.<ref>{{cite book |first=W. |last=Pratt |first2=T. |last2=Cooper |first3=I. |last3=Kabir |chapter=Pseudomedian filter |title=Architectures and Algorithms for Digital Image Processing II |pages=34–43 |series=Proc. SPIE |volume=534 |year=1985 |doi=10.1117/12.946562 }}</ref>
